en: Theragāthā 5.12 Pañcakanipāta First Chapter (Paṭhamavagga)
The Verse of the Elder Kosiya:
“The wise man who indeed understands the words of his elders,
And dwells with them, should generate affection for them.”
Thus one becomes both devoted and wise;
having understood the nature of phenomena, one becomes distinguished.
When great calamities arise—
One who does not lean on the pillars of night and reflects with discernment is called strong and wise;
having understood things as they are, he becomes distinguished among all phenomena.
He who stands like the ocean, unshaken,
with profound wisdom and insight into subtle meanings—
he is called a wise man, one who cannot be led astray.
Having known, he becomes distinguished among things.
He is one of great learning who upholds the Dhamma,
and he is a practitioner of the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma.
Thus he is indeed wise and becomes distinguished among all things after having understood them;
he who understands the meaning of what is spoken—
Having understood the goal, he acts accordingly;
such a wise man is called one who has transcended the ordinary,
for having understood the phenomena, he becomes distinguished among them.
… The Elder Kosiya … The Fifth Chapter is finished.
Herein is the summary verse:
Rājadatta and Subhūta,
Girimānanda and Sumana,
and the elder Vaḍḍha Kassapa.
Gayākassapa and Vakkali,
Vijita and Yasadatta,
and Soṇa who is called Kosiya;
There are sixty-five verses,
and twelve elders are mentioned therein.
